The laboratory smelled of solder and burnt coffee. Priya adjusted the oscilloscope, watched the waveform settle into a tremulous sine, and allowed herself a small, sardonic smile. Three months of recalcitrant hardware, of intermittent faults that vanished whenever anyone came to look, and now the circuit behaved with an almost obsequious punctuality. She did not trust it. Experience had taught her that a system which worked the first time was merely waiting for a demonstration in front of the funding committee before it failed in some new and ingenious way. She wrote everything down, photographed the bench, and went home before the luck could change. On the third day the fog lifted and the archipelago appeared, a scattering of green islands on a pewter sea. The captain, a phlegmatic Scot who had sailed these waters for thirty years, pointed out the reefs with the stem of his pipe and named each island as if introducing old acquaintances.
